text:
marta-docs: Quick note — the sampleapp's chat streaming section is confusing new users. The REST example uses streaming (SSE) and the SDK example in the repo returns a full message then closes. New user filed an issue in the tutorial.

liam-sdk: Can you paste the exact curl vs SDK snippets? I haven't seen a behavioral diff on our side recently.

marta-docs: Repro: curl (works as SSE):
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/chat?stream=true'
# yields chunked SSE events, keeps connection open
```

Node SDK (sampleapp code):
```
const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-chat', messages, stream: true });
for await (const chunk of res) {
  // only one chunk then iterator stops
}
```

liam-sdk: Ack. I tried locally — SDK yields one combined chunk then finishes. Looks like our http client treats `stream` boolean specially in query building: if stream === true we set `Accept: text/event-stream`, but if stream === true it also toggles `socket.endOnFinish=true` in the old http adapter. Oops.

adarsh-backend: On the server we stream SSE whenever query param `stream=true`. If the connection is closed early we log a client disconnect. We're not force-closing. If the SDK closes, server's fine.

jen-qa: I hit this in onboarding e2e: sampleapp expects streaming partial tokens for the UI typing effect. With the SDK behavior the UI flashes full response at once which looks broken for users. This is causing a flaky failing test in the tutorial CI.

liam-sdk: Two problems here: 1) serializer/adapter toggles socket behavior for stream=true, and 2) our retry layer treats a single 200 with no subsequent chunks as a recoverable short-circuit and immediately retries the request, which can lead to duplicate messages in some clients. I'll open a fix.

marta-docs: Also noticed the python sample used stream: "true" (string) which worked — so there's a cross-language parity issue: python and REST ok, node not. We should add a note in the Quickstart until fixed.

liam-sdk: Plan: patch node adapter to not set endOnFinish when Accept is text/event-stream; preserve connection until server closes. Ensure serializer keeps boolean true/false as booleans (don't stringify). Also change retry logic: don't retry on 200 if response had content-type starting with text/event-stream or transfer-encoding: chunked. Add unit + integration tests that assert streaming iterator yields multiple chunks for long responses.

adarsh-backend: On our side we can add a temporary safeguard: when we see stream=true but client indicates early close, we can emit a log and set a short retry-after header so clients see deterministic behavior. But this is temporary.

jen-qa: I'll add a test that launches the sampleapp, mocks a slow stream (5 chunks over 3s) and asserts the UI gets incremental updates. I'll also add an automation that uses the SDK call directly (both int and string variants) so we catch param-typing drift.

liam-sdk: Created branch sdk/fix-stream-adapter-211 and PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/211. Patch includes adapter change, serializer fix, tests, and a small docs note.

ci-bot: CI triggered for sdk/fix-stream-adapter-211 (checks: unit, node-integration, python-compat).

marta-docs: Thanks — can we get a tiny docs patch in the sampleapp repo to show both curl and SDK workarounds (`stream: 'true'` as a temporary note)? New users are hitting this during the quickstart.

liam-sdk: Yep will add a line and link to the changelog. After merge we should retire the temporary docs note.

jen-qa: Marking this thread for follow-up: once PR merges I'll update the sampleapp CI expectation and unblock the tutorial failing tests.

marta-docs: Great, leaving this open until the tests pass and sampleapp updated. Cheers :sparkles:
